method: Automated inventory read every source, evidence, pathway, profile and review record in the exact manifest candidate for this ISO.

Automated screening compared source references, locators, geography fields, evidence class, direction, status, horizon and scenario; it checked pathway support IDs, link-evidence sets, geography fields, alternatives and uncertainty for follow-up.

Raw extraction access rows are recorded only as inherited access observations. This generated screen does not treat snippets, HTTP success, prior access, or metadata as claim verification and does not replace semantic source review.

audit_access_attempt.locator: Methods: Data and Analysis; Results Table 2; Discussion limitations

evidence.compact_statement: Source dated 2024-12-17 reports: The district assessment placed 51 districts in very high and 118 in high flood-risk bands; about 85% of those districts are in Assam, Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, West Bengal, Gujarat, Odisha and Jammu and Kashmir.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

evidence.compact_statement: Source dated 2024-12-17 reports: The assessment placed 91 districts in very high and 188 in high drought-risk bands; more than 85% of these districts are in Bihar, Assam, Jharkhand, Odisha, Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, West Bengal, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Chhattisgarh, Kerala, Uttarakhand and Haryana.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

evidence.compact_statement: Source dated 2024-12-17 reports: Among the 50 districts with highest flood risk and 50 with highest drought risk, 11 were very high risk for both, including Patna, Alappuzha, Charaideo, Dibrugarh, Sibsagar, South Salmara-Mankachar, Golaghat, Kendrapara, Murshidabad, Nadia and Uttar Dinajpur.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

evidence.compact_statement: Source dated 2025-05-20 reports: CEEW classed 417 of 734 districts (57%), home to 76% of residents, at high or very high heat risk; Delhi, Maharashtra, Goa, Kerala and Gujarat ranked among the highest-risk states.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

evidence.compact_statement: Source dated 2025-05-20 reports: Comparing 2012–2022 with 1982–2011, CEEW found extra warm nights per summer in Mumbai (15), Bengaluru (11), Bhopal and Jaipur (7 each), Delhi (6) and Chennai (4); warm nights rose faster than hot days.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

evidence.compact_statement: Source dated 2025-05-20 reports: CEEW found high heat vulnerability in districts of seven named states, where heat combined with chronic illness, older people and under-fives; Odisha districts with green cover and blue infrastructure had lower vulnerability.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

evidence.compact_statement: Source dated 2026-07-20 reports: By July 2026, heat action plans were reported for 23 states, 195 districts and 64 cities; national guidance recommends that plans protect street vendors and other outdoor workers through shade, hydration, cooling spaces, flexible hours and alerts.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

evidence.scenario: The release reports about +1.5°C under SSP2-4.5 and up to +2.1°C under SSP5-8.5 by mid-century.
evidence.compact_statement: Source dated 2026-07-20 reports: Delhi's SAPCC 2.0 assessment identifies South Delhi as most and New Delhi as least climate-vulnerable; it projects higher summer maximum temperatures and more very hot days by mid-century, with cool roofs, cooling corridors, green infrastructure, drainage and wetland measures envisaged.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

evidence.compact_statement: Source dated 2025-05-01 reports: NHRC cited 3,798 NCRB-recorded heat and sun-stroke deaths in 2018–2022 and identified economically weaker people, outdoor workers, older people, children and homeless people as at risk from inadequate shelter and resources; it urged 11 states to provide protections.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

evidence.compact_statement: The 2023 study reports drought–IPV associations, not causation. Precipitation analysis used 122,696 married women across NFHS 2015–16 and 2019–21; government-declared socioeconomic drought analysis used 62,464 women in NFHS 2015–16 only. Adjusted odds ratios vary by drought definition and violence type.
recommendations: Keep the numerical and association summary provisional until the full article or publisher-authorized copy is accessible; do not claim this audit verified its estimates.
